chapter: CBS, return to Ellington and retirement
title: Returning to Ellington in 1960
summary: Brown found his distinctive tone did not fit the studio and was glad to rejoin for travel and Europe.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yes, 1960 I went back in with Ellington which was -- you see, when you jump into the studio type playing, it's more or less of -- for instance, a trombone player which was the instrument I had -- they all had the same tone usually. One could be off, and another step right into that same structure and sound just like the other one sounds, see.

Well, I wasn't too good at that. I had been with Ellington too long, and I had a certain sound. And I didn't think it fit so well. So, I was sort of glad to get out of the studio because I never tried first parts. I usually tried backup parts such as second, third, or fourth trombone parts. And I had a peculiar tone that I didn't think fit much of anything.
Which Duke was glad to get back, right?
I don't know, but I went back and did some more traveling, some more one nighters, plenty of Europe, and stuff I'd been used to.
